title: Working several bands at once; Joe Howard and the 1915 storm
summary: Barnes was in a regular band with Clem while also working for Joe Howard and others, around the time of the 1915 storm.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah. Six piece, five, six pieces, Clem. I just can't remember them. Was it a regular band really? Were the same guys at every job almost or was it just kind of a different pick up bands?
No, it was a regular band. A regular band. Yeah. A regular band. And how long did you stay with Clem?

Well I'll tell you how it's what, if he'd have it, when he'd be working he'd call us to get something, he'd call us Don't Touch Nuthin' for a second, fifth a time. You understand? I see. Well that's his men, he'd get them in together and then they'd get it. So you'd be working with other bands at the same time? I'd be working with, in fact I'd be working with many bands. And when I was working with him, I'd be working with Joe Howard and, uh, and, uh, and, uh, uh, Raleigh, uh, the Dixie Clubers.

I'd be working with Joe Howard and, uh, I'd be working with Joe Howard. Joe Howard was a leader? Yeah. What did he play then? How? He played trumpet. Did he play trumpet? Yeah. Now, uh, let me see. You must have been in your twenties by now, huh? Well I'm in five years, I don't know. Yeah, it's hard to keep it all strange. Well, who are you? Well, about England.
Yeah, I'm pretty sure. Was that before the big storm or after? Before the big storm?
That was after. After? No. That's 1915 that storm. Yeah, that was the place where he was killing.
And then after the band that I played more with than anybody.
Than any other. Any other. Did you go with him after you left Clem, would you say?
I mean you were playing mostly with Clem, and then the next one you played mostly with Clem?
No, I played with Clem before I played with him.
Yeah, but then after Clem it was Kelly?
